bug_semantics: Bastillion's authentication filter was mapped only to /manage/* and /admin/*, while the lmvc controller dispatcher accepted any raw request URI containing an annotated controller path plus .ktrl. A request such as /anything/manage/viewUsers.ktrl therefore missed the prefix-scoped AuthFilter but was still substring-dispatched to the privileged /manage/viewUsers controller; unauthenticated attackers could read administrative data, create a MANAGER account, and register systems.
flaw_origin: The flawed routing primitive was first written in the lmvc framework's 2018 initial source commit: BaseKontroller.execute() used request.getRequestURI().contains(c.path() + DispatcherServlet.CTR_EXT). Bastillion first integrated that framework in 65475902748be6b86a95d17b8409518697fe1e77 while retaining prefix-only AuthFilter mappings, making the mismatch exploitable in the application. Later package renames, artifact releases, and the 2026 source import merely carried the same line forward.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object identifies author and committer as Sean Kavanagh <sean.p.kavanagh6@gmail.com>, has subject/body exactly 'Initial commit', and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other trailers.
evidence: First-party issue https://github.com/bastillion-io/Bastillion/issues/669 documents the pre-auth path-prefix bypass, reproduces /anything/manage/viewUsers.ktrl returning the user list and /x/manage/saveUser.ktrl creating a manager without credentials, and reports validation against lmvc 2.0.0. At tag v5.1.0 (af829d231902574eaf56b3f8b913e4179ff5c79a), src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml maps AuthFilter only to /manage/* and /admin/* and DispatcherServlet to *.ktrl; src/main/java/loophole/mvc/base/BaseKontroller.java dispatches with request.getRequestURI().contains(c.path() + DispatcherServlet.CTR_EXT). The published lmvc-2.0.0-sources.jar contains that same statement, and its POM names the now-removed https://github.com/bastillion-io/lmvc SCM. Git -S over the preserved original lmvc history (https://github.com/lizhonghao2/lmvc) and both pre/post-rename paths identifies bedbbd5945a57abbefdaa1d71eb5ce76d80f3fa8 as the sole addition of getRequestURI().contains; bfbfd89449b2f7441466fcbe770da57fbfd930bb is only the com.lmvc-to-loophole.mvc package rename, and Bastillion commit fbfd6639227ee8a8f858229191c1639490a2618c is a later source import, so neither is the BIC. `git cat-file commit bedbbd...` gives immediate parent 4524a69036b627ceca788bf5fdc7779121dd569c; `git cat-file -e 4524a...:src/main/java/com/lmvc/base/BaseKontroller.java` fails and `git ls-tree -r --name-only 4524a...` lists only LICENSE, directly proving parent-tree absence. Bastillion commit 65475902748be6b86a95d17b8409518697fe1e77 first replaces Struts with loophole.mvc:lmvc 1.00.00 and preserves the two prefix-only AuthFilter mappings; it is absent from v2.90.03 but is an ancestor of v3.00.00 (764778b16d81197fe82a55274e83523d8591a263), establishing the application boundary. VulnCheck's advisory states Bastillion <=5.1.0 is affected. Direct fix d759fb686a1a097b1b026e286fd9b20e5ba349c8 changes BaseKontroller to exact request.getServletPath().equals(...) routing (and aligns AuthFilter with getServletPath()); its immediate parent 4a63f4d2f10bc7d02d65cfd2848c4b0d17d6b98 still has the vulnerable statement. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` shows the fix is not in v5.1.0 but is in patched tag v5.2.0 (68a09811c7f0f0ad20369f31e3de82d15dd80e3a).
reasoning: The security boundary and the router disagreed about path identity: the servlet container decided whether to invoke AuthFilter from the leading normalized mapping, but lmvc independently searched the entire raw URI for a controller substring. Prefixing a privileged controller path therefore skipped authentication without preventing controller execution. History reconstruction follows the vulnerable line past Bastillion's 2026 vendor import and lmvc's 2018 package rename to bedbbd5945a57abbefdaa1d71eb5ce76d80f3fa8, the smallest commit that actually wrote the contains-based dispatcher. Its direct parent has no BaseKontroller file or vulnerable line. The framework BIC predates Bastillion's v3.00.00 integration, the line remains in affected v5.1.0, and d759fb686a1a097b1b026e286fd9b20e5ba349c8 replaces it with normalized exact matching in v5.2.0. AI attribution is judged only from the BIC object; that object has a human author/committer and no AI marker, so later Claude co-authorship on the fix is irrelevant and the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
